relevance.rationale: Join CORRECT (arXiv:1208.1663v2, Garoufalidis, 'The 3D index of an ideal triangulation and angle structures', with an appendix by S. Zwegers; matches the registered entry's author, year and URL). Cited at three Lean sites - lean/QOU/Knot/SymmetricOptimum.lean:46, L6a4AngleStructure.lean:58, M004AngleStructure.lean:63 - each as '-- Ref: [garoufalidis2012] arXiv:1208.1663 Sec. 2.2-2.3 (generalised angle structures)', and regenerated from computations/probes/gen_l6a4_angle_structure_lean.py:111. The locator is ACCURATE and load-bearing: Sec. 2.2 of this document is titled 'Angle structures' and defines a generalized angle structure on a combinatorial ideal tetrahedron as an assignment of angles summing to 1 at each vertex, determined by a triple (alpha, beta, gamma) in R^3 with alpha + beta + gamma = 1, and calls it strict when all three are positive; Sec. 2.3 supplies the Neumann-Zagier matrices. That is exactly the object the three Lean modules manipulate. Scope note on what is NOT claimed: SymmetricOptimum.lean is explicit that it proves only the symmetry half (orbit averaging, convexity, Jensen) and nothing about uniqueness of the symmetric point or about hyperbolic volume - so the citation is used at the right strength, not overreached.

keyResults.locator: Sec. 2.2 (Def. of generalized angle structure); Sec. 2.3 (Neumann-Zagier matrices)
keyResults.statement: A generalized angle structure on an ideal tetrahedron is a triple (alpha, beta, gamma) in R^3 with alpha + beta + gamma = 1, strict when all are positive; index structures are a generalization of strict angle structures, and the domain of the 3D index is exactly the triangulations supporting an index structure.
keyResults.useForFolio: Sources the angle-structure polytope the SymmetricOptimum / L6a4 / M004 modules argue over, including the linear constraint that makes the feasible set convex - which is what the Jensen/orbit-averaging argument needs.
